blocks.text: # What our local Proofpress experiments actually showed

**Status:** comprehensive local-results synthesis through 2026-08-12. This document covers the full `experiments/provenance_handoff` experiment lineage. The main body presents the research story and product conclusions; run-level details, invalid paths, exclusions, repairs, and unexecuted protocols are confined to the appendices.
## The question behind the experiments

AI agents do not only need memory. They need a way to decide whether inherited work is still admissible: which artifact and evidence it came from, whether it was accepted or superseded, and what must be reopened when the world changes. Across our local studies, we tested three progressively narrower questions: can provenance travel through an agent workflow; does it improve task quality or continuity; and does executable artifact binding prevent stale work from being reused against the wrong revision?
## The short answer

The broad “better provenance makes agents produce better work” hypothesis did not hold consistently. Clean-task quality was usually tied, mixed, or limited by the underlying task and harness. The narrower admission-control hypothesis held much more reliably: when ordinary and Proofpress handoffs carried the same readable decision state, native version binding repeatedly changed the receiver's behavior under stale or decision-relevant drift while preserving clean or irrelevant-change continuation in the qualified slices.

The result is best understood as a product boundary. Proofpress is not a replacement for shared memory, source access, good handoff writing, or semantic judgment. It is an admission and audit layer for portable work: it makes inherited state inspectable, binds it to an artifact lineage, and gives the receiver a deterministic reason to continue, revalidate, or refuse.
## What held up across the experiment program

| Finding | Evidence across local studies | Current interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Transport and native carriers are feasible | Receiver-only, sidecar, document-native, Gateway, OpenRouter, Claude CLI, DOCX, and Proofpress carrier paths all produced working records in at least one qualified slice | The product can move through heterogeneous agent workflows; transport feasibility alone is not efficacy |
| Clean output quality did not show a general uplift | Sidecar workflows, DeepSeek/GLM Harvey slices, APEX Law, Restricted Lease, Artifact Travel, Policy, HiEviDR, and Knowledge Handoff often tied or showed no consistent C2 advantage | Do not market Proofpress as a generic quality booster |
| Stale-binding admission is the strongest repeatable mechanism | APEX-direct, Luna confirmatory, three-model replication, HiEviDR R1, and Knowledge Handoff Track 2 showed large or complete separation when the fault was not otherwise resolved | Proofpress can reliably govern whether inherited work remains admissible on the tested fixtures |
| Visible evidence changes the benefit | HiEviDR R2 and both Policy R1 slices had zero unsafe propagation in ordinary and Proofpress arms; Proofpress changed revalidation behavior rather than final safety | Binding is most valuable when a stale basis would otherwise remain plausible or hidden |
| Portable provenance reasoning remains measurement-sensitive | STALE/CUPMem showed `P3−P2 +8.33pp` with Nano, but `−1.67pp` and `−2.08pp` with two Gemini passes | The STALE effect is judge-sensitive and cannot support a judge-independent efficacy claim |
| Handoff itself reduces rediscovery | Knowledge Handoff Track 1 found rediscovery in H0 `3/3` and in H1/H2 `0/3` | A readable handoff has immediate continuity value; stronger H2 structure has not yet beaten prose H1 |
## 1. Early work established feasibility, not product advantage

The first experiments showed that agent teams could emit, transport, and consume provenance records across fresh sessions and multi-stage workflows. The isolated handoff diagnostic completed 24 receiver calls, and the external-sidecar prototype completed 36/36 workflows. But the quality comparisons were mixed and the treatment was not yet the native product: in the sidecar study, memory and provenance arms were close for DeepSeek and Luna, while Muse favored memory. Later DeepSeek and GLM Harvey slices similarly found near-identical criterion scores between ordinary coordination and Proofpress-enhanced coordination, sometimes at substantially higher multi-agent cost. These studies justified building the native carrier; they did not justify an efficacy claim.
## 2. Portable provenance showed a real but unstable reasoning signal

MemConflict reduced stale/regression errors from `12.5%` with ordinary memory to `4.2%` with Proofpress, but trusted success was tied at `83.3%` and task success was lower for Proofpress (`87.5%` versus `95.8%`). STALE/CUPMem then produced a positive portable-carrier contrast under the preregistered Nano scorer: P3 scored `146/240` versus P2 `126/240`, a paired `+8.33pp` with 95% CI `[+1.25pp, +15.42pp]`. Two Gemini rescoring passes on the same frozen answers produced `−1.67pp` and `−2.08pp`. The disagreement audit traced much of the reversal to how judges score grounded abstention. The honest conclusion is not “the effect disappeared,” but that the current effect cannot be separated from the evaluation policy.
## 3. Full portable handoff packages did not improve clean task completion

The APEX Law public-source comparison tied ordinary and Proofpress handoffs exactly: both scored `14/18` on the native rubric and `15/21` on the blind audit. The Restricted-Access Lease study was also effectively tied: the frozen audit was `13/21` each, while a diagnostic post-hoc audit was `17/21` versus `16/21`, driven by one terminology cell. Artifact Travel v2 and the replicated v3 matrix likewise found zero clean trusted completions in every arm; v3's paired C2-versus-C1 result was one C2 win, two C1 wins, and 15 ties. These studies were valuable negative evidence: richer lineage and verification cannot rescue a workflow whose clean task contract, source boundary, or final document execution is itself weak.
## 4. Receive-time binding produced the clearest causal pattern

In the corrected APEX-direct Claude replication, all arms admitted clean work `12/12`, while stale fault behavior separated completely: C0 and C1 made `12/12` unsafe proceeds and C2 made `0/12`. The preregistered Luna confirmatory study reproduced `12/12` versus `0/12`, and a separate three-model follow-up reproduced the same pattern for GLM 5.2, Kimi K3, and Qwen 3.8 Max: descriptively, C1 made `36/36` stale unsafe proceeds and C2 made `0/36`, with clean admission `36/36` in each arm. This is the strongest result in the local program, while remaining bounded to a design-aligned APEX-derived fixture.

The more natural revision tasks add an important qualification. HiEviDR R1 also separated completely on a near-current wrong-synthesis binding: C2 was safe `9/9`, C1 unsafe `9/9`. But when R2 made the semantic contradiction visible in the current evidence, both arms had zero unsafe propagation; C2 consistently reverified while C1 self-corrected in four cases and explicitly recovered in five. The Policy R1 Claude and Luna slices showed the same pattern: both arms were safe, but C2 used provenance-triggered revalidation `9/9` while C1 self-corrected `9/9`. Proofpress therefore affects the recovery path even when it does not change the final safety rate.
## 5. Knowledge Handoff connected the mechanism to a simple product story

Track 1 showed the continuity value of any competent handoff: across three DeepSeek fixtures, artifact-only H0 rediscovered a source in `3/3`, while prose H1 and structured H2 did so in `0/3`. Track 2 isolated version binding. Both repaired GLM 5.2 and DeepSeek runs produced the same aggregate two-state result: V1 proceeded on all irrelevant edits and targeted revalidation on all relevant edits; V0 proceeded on two of three relevant edits for each model. Across the repeated same-fixture slices, V1 was `6/6` on harmless proceed and `6/6` on relevant revalidation, while V0 continued on `4/6` relevant-edit responses.
## The product claim we can make

**Proofpress gives successor agents a portable, independently checkable admission layer for inherited work. Local experiments show that ordinary handoffs already help continuity and can self-correct when current evidence is obvious. Proofpress's distinctive value appears when the receiver must determine whether that inherited state still belongs to the current artifact: on the tested stale-binding and version-drift fixtures, native binding made that decision more consistent and auditable without requiring blanket rejection of harmless changes.**

What we should not claim is equally clear. The local program has not established a general improvement in task quality, a real-world effect size, official APEX or HiEviDR benchmark performance, legal or factual truth, or superiority to full shared memory. The strongest experiments validate a bounded admission mechanism; the broader product benefit still depends on task design, source visibility, handoff quality, and the cost of selective recovery.

## Appendix B — invalid, excluded, stopped, and repaired paths

- Early DeepInfra Harvey attempts exceeded endpoint completion limits or stalled; the later Novita slice remained separate and Phase 2 stopped incomplete after SSL, BrokenPipe, 429, and long-synthesis failures.
- Gateway Harvey v1 sent an object-shaped reasoning option to an adapter requiring a scalar value. The immutable v2 reran from a fresh root; transient scorer 500s were preserved and retried without fallback.
- STALE's primary Nano result failed two Gemini judge-robustness passes. The audit localized disagreement to the rubric treatment of grounded abstention; no 400-scenario scale-up was authorized.
- The first Restricted-Access Lease run leaked an original source filename; another stopped on a Gateway tool-schema abort. Both were excluded before the corrected pilot and formal slice.
- APEX-direct v1 exposed a harness-only synthetic `capsule.json` to C2. Its apparent clean false stop was induced by packaging, so the clean-path estimate was invalidated while the fault observation remained descriptive.
- Artifact Travel v2 used direct Gemini for C0 and Gateway for C1/C2, confounding C0 comparisons. Artifact Travel v3 repaired transport parity but still produced zero clean completion because the operative DOCX task failed.
- Artifact Travel v4 retained missing reviewer event files despite complete cost ledgers. V5 was invalid because `PROOFPRESS_CLI` was unset and required C2 verification never ran. V6 completed 36 cells but has no registered canonical efficacy analysis and many missing fault dispositions.
- The APEX-direct Claude replication replaced seven attempts that omitted the output contract. HiEviDR R1 replaced two missing-contract C1 faults; R2 replaced one Haiku-contaminated trace.
- Luna confirmatory APEX retained four TLS/output-contract exclusions and replacements within the declared cap. The Policy analyzer's first post-run summary used a stale denominator and was versioned rather than overwritten.
- GLM Knowledge Handoff Track 2 reran all six V1 cells after discovering a missing checkpoint and reran one timed-out V0 cell. Early DeepSeek Track 1 runs failed because an overlong Gateway correlation value produced HTTP 400; only the repaired r4 roots enter the result.
## Appendix C — evidence classes and non-pooling rules

Transport qualifications, raw completed matrices, local diagnostics, preregistered confirmatory slices, external-benchmark adaptations, and independent-fixture studies answer different questions. Their denominators are never added into one product-effect sample size. Repeated calls on one fixture measure receiver reliability, not task diversity. A valid carrier proves identity, integrity, and declared lineage; it does not prove that the source claim is true, current, authorized, or legally correct. Post-hoc audits may diagnose measurement problems but do not replace frozen primary endpoints.
